_note: Live-reporting scenarios for the Central Asia edition. Real references (2024 Kazakhstan floods, 1887/1911 Almaty earthquakes, 2025-2026 Tashkent heat waves) anchor the numbers; exposure fractions, timings, shelters, supplies and company sites are labelled assumptions.

scenarios.name_ja: Almaty M7.3 earthquake (Verny-type, Trans-Ili Alatau front)
scenarios.desc_ja: Scenario: a M7.3 Verny-type earthquake on the Trans-Ili Alatau frontal fault zone just south of Almaty (the 1887 source area), at 10:40 on a weekday in late November. MSK IX-X in the foothill districts (Nauryzbay, Bostandyk, Medeu), IX in the centre and on the soft, water-saturated loess plain of the north (Almaly, Alatau, Zhetysu), VIII-IX in Auezov, Turksib and Talgar, VIII in Karasay, VII-VIII in Ile. Soviet-era brick and panel housing collapses, gas fires, loss of power, water and district heating with frost at night, and a M6.0 aftershock at 36 h. Intensities, exposure fractions and timings are assumptions built on the 2020-21 microzonation (whole city in the MSK 9-10 zone), the 2017-18 seismic certification (19% of floor area needs strengthening, 12% slated for demolition) and the January 2024 M7.0 reaction (mass night-time egress into the cold).
scenarios.t0_ja: t=0: Thursday 19 Nov 2026, 10:40 local (+05:00), M7.3 main shock (assumed)
scenarios.agency_ja: Institute of Seismology (Almaty) / Ministry of Emergency Situations
scenarios.kpi_dead_note_ja: Refs: 1887 Verny 332 dead, 1911 Kemin 452 dead (city then under 50k); Amey et al. 2021: 4,100 +/- 3,500 deaths for a M6.5 under today's city; experts: up to 30% of buildings destroyed at MSK IX-X. Rate 0.003 assumed; demo model
assumptions_ja: District populations: 2021 census district counts (citypopulation.de) scaled x1.123 to the 2024-11-01 city total of 2,280,296 (stat.gov.kz); Talgar 265k (akim, 2025); Karasay and Ile grown from 2013 census figures (assumed).
jp = expatriate residents per district: no published figure; values are order-of-magnitude assumptions concentrated in Medeu (Samal, Dostyk), Bostandyk (Koktem, Esentai) and Almaly.

Exposure fractions follow the assumed MSK intensity by district (foothill source zone vs loess/high-groundwater north) and building stock (self-built, 1950s-70s brick, large-panel, modern RC); no official microzonation polygons were available.
fatality_rate 0.003 sits between the historical city tolls (1887: 332; 1911: 452) and Amey et al. 2021 (4,100 +/- 3,500 for a M6.5 under the city); the model total is a demo, not a forecast.

Shelter capacities, utility restoration times, logistics states, supply stocks, company sites (staff, locations) and all t-values are assumptions; the real references are the 2024-01-23 reaction (384 reception points opened within 1-1.5 h, some closed), the 2024-03-04 metro inspection (5 h) and MES mobilization plans (55,000 personnel).

scenarios.supply_note_ja: Cold-season earthquake: the first 24 h are dominated by trauma kits, search-and-rescue and blankets (frost at night), from 48 h by winterized tents, heaters, hygiene kits and water. Demand = evacuees x per-person rate; supply = stock plus an arrival curve. All stocks and lead times are assumptions; references: MES plan to mobilize 55,000 personnel and 9,000 equipment units within 24-72 h, and relief items reaching the January 2024 epicentre within about 12 h.

scenarios.name_ja: West Kazakhstan spring flood on the Zhem and Zhaiyk rivers (2024-type scenario)
scenarios.desc_ja: Two-river spring flood of the 2024 type. Snowmelt on frozen ground sends the Zhem (Emba) through Kulsary within hours, cutting the Atyrau-Tengiz road and displacing more than half the town, while a record release from the Iriklinskoye reservoir in Russia drives a slow Zhaiyk (Ural) wave past Uralsk, Inderbor and Makhambet towards Atyrau, where 252 km of dams defend a city 20 m below sea level. For the 7-day live window the Zhaiyk wave is compressed about 6-fold (2024: Uralsk peak 22 Apr, Inderbor 13 May, Atyrau 30 May to 3 Jun).

scenarios.desc_ja: Uzhydromet warns of 41-44 C daytime heat for about a week, modelled on the July 2025 and July 2026 heat waves (Tashkent 44.3 C on 2026-07-19, 0.3 C below the 1997 record). Risks are heat illness, rolling power outages as air-conditioning load peaks, and low water pressure; no damage model applies (watch-type scenario).
